person.description: The account that accepted the invite, when the identity service names it.

state.description: `pending` until a person signs in at the app with the address, `active` after.

agent.description: The copy in the Agents API.

version.description: The copy's version in the Agents API, which a new session runs.

model.description: The routed name of the Effort level a session of the copy starts at.

version.description: The managed agent's version the copy carries: the live one.

Bookmarks.description: The turns the person bookmarked in the token's context, by session. Each context keeps its own bookmarks.

max_per_session.description: The most turns one session holds bookmarked.

max_sessions.description: The most sessions a context holds bookmarks in.

sessions.description: Each session's id and the sequences of its bookmarked turns, ascending.

amount_micro.description: What the person pays, in micro-USD.

cancel_url.description: Where the payment page sends the person when they leave without paying, on the origin of a Latere product.

success_url.description: Where the payment page sends the person once they paid: an absolute address on the origin of a Latere product.

DataPreferences.description: The person's own data section, in every context they work in, and who holds Zero data retention on in the token's context.

zero_retention.description: The person's own Zero data retention, `false` until the person sets it. While it is on, the model requests of the person's sessions, of their own API keys and of Parsing in their personal context go only to endpoints whose terms keep nothing of them, by each model's data terms: a model such an endpoint serves runs through it alone, and a model none serves is not available, so a level with no other is refused `zero_retention`, and a change to such a model and a message into a session on one are refused `zero_retention`; Auto's decisions about the person's messages go only to such endpoints too. A session that took it keeps it until the session ends, the setting turned off or not; a key is released when it is turned off. It is the person's own choice: in an organization's context, the organization's setting can hold Zero data retention on while this reads `false` (see `zero_retention_by`).

zero_retention_by.description: Present while Zero data retention is on for the person in the token's context: `organization` while the context's organization keeps it on, which it does until an owner or an admin turns it off, whatever the person chose, so a client shows the person's switch on and not theirs to change there; `person` while only the person's own setting holds it.

zero_retention_routes.description: `true`: Zero data retention sends a session's model requests only to endpoints that keep nothing of them, closing only a model no such endpoint serves, rather than closing every model one of whose endpoints may keep a request. A client offers the setting where this is `true`.

Device.description: One of the person's computers, connected as an environment the sessions they start work on.

folders.description: The folders the computer lets a session work in, read-only unless `write` is true. Empty until it has connected.

id.description: The computer's id, which is also its environment's name in Environments.

isolation.description: How a session's commands are confined on the computer: `process`, the operating system's sandbox, which keeps them to the granted folders.

last_seen.description: When the computer was last heard from.

network.description: The network the computer allows a session: `none`; `allowlist` and the hosts it names; or `open`, any public host but those `blocked` names, where `hosts` are the ports beyond 443 and 80 it admits, each as `host:port`. Under `open`, anything a session can read in the computer's folders can be sent to any public host.

blocked.description: The hosts a computer on `open` blocks: a host, an address, or `*.example.com` for the names below it, alone or as `host:port`. Empty under the other modes.

os.description: The operating system the computer reports while it is connected, such as `darwin` or `linux`. Absent until it has connected.

status.description: `online` while the computer serves its environment, `offline` while it does not, and `unknown` when its state could not be read.

EffortAuto.description: Auto, present while the installation offers it: the routed name that picks Quick or Thorough for each message. A client shows Auto only while this member is present.

asks.description: Present while Auto may ask before a level it does not run by itself: `sustained`, while Auto reads the message and Sustained can run for the caller. A client marks a message `askable` only while this member holds the level.

available.description: Whether a message sent on Auto now would run for the caller: whether one of the levels it picks among is available.

levels.description: The ids of the levels Auto picks among, least effort first.

name.description: The routed name a session's model is given for Auto.

reads.description: How Auto reads a message: `message`, by what it asks, where the installation chose a decision model that reads it; `shape`, by its length, its files and its links.

reason.description: Present when Auto is not available, that is when neither level can run: `budget_exhausted` when a level is closed because the wallet of the caller's context has spent past its credit, else `model_tier_auto_unavailable`, the refusal a message gets then. Quick's free models stay open on a spent wallet, so Auto stays available while they run.

retention.description: Whether Auto's decision about a message of the caller's may be kept: `provider` while the decision model reading it may keep a request, `none` otherwise, which it is while Auto reads the shape alone or Zero data retention is on for the caller in the token's context.

available.description: Whether a message sent on the level now would be routed for the caller.

models.description: The models the level may run for the caller, in the level's order of preference: its pool as the caller's own narrowing leaves it, of what the caller's context is offered. Empty where the level runs nothing for the caller.

name.description: The routed name a session's model is given for the level, `tier/<id>`. `tier/<id>/<model>` chooses one of the level's `models`.

order.description: The level's place, least effort first, from 0.

reason.description: Present when the level is not available: the refusal a message would get. `zero_retention` when Zero data retention is on for the caller in the token's context and no model of the level is served by an endpoint that keeps nothing; `model_tier_<id>_unavailable` when the level can run no model for the caller in the context now; `rate_limited` when only free models could run it and the free turns are used for now, by the caller today or by everyone this minute or today; and `budget_exhausted` when the wallet of the caller's context has spent past its credit, which closes every level until credit is added.

resets_at.description: Present when `reason` is `rate_limited`: when the bound reached opens again, the moment a message's refusal names. The next minute for the bound on everyone's free turns a minute, else the next UTC day.

retention.description: Whether a request on the level can be kept. `none` when no provider of any model the level may run for the caller's context keeps a request, or, while Zero data retention is on, when the level runs, its requests going only to such providers; `provider` when one may keep it under its own terms. Absent when that is not known for every such model, or the level may run none.

zero_retention.description: Whether Zero data retention is on for the caller in the token's context: a session's model requests go only to endpoints whose terms keep nothing of them, so every model such an endpoint serves runs and reads `retention: none`, and a model no such endpoint serves reads `available: false` with `reason` `zero_retention`, as does a level with no other. It is on while the context's organization keeps it on, which it does until an owner or an admin turns it off, or while the caller turned on their own; the stricter of the two holds. A session that took it keeps it until the session ends.

zero_retention_by.description: Present while `zero_retention` is `true`: who holds it on. `organization` while the context's organization keeps it on, whether or not the caller turned on their own; the caller cannot turn it off for themselves there. `person` while only the caller's own setting holds it.

EffortModel.description: One model a level lists for the caller, which the routed name `tier/<id>/<name>` chooses.

available.description: Whether a message on the level with this model chosen would run now.

charge.description: `none` for a free model, whose turns count against the level's free turns; `credit` for a model with a price, charged to the wallet of the caller's context.

free_again_at.description: With `rate_limited`: when the free turns open again.

name.description: The model's name in the catalog.

provider.description: The name a person reads for the provider that serves the model, such as `Anthropic` or `OpenRouter`, which tells apart two models of one vendor served two ways. Absent when the catalog names none.

reason.description: Present when the model is not available: `zero_retention` while Zero data retention is on for the caller in the token's context and no endpoint that keeps nothing serves the model, `model_tier_model_unavailable` when it cannot run now, `rate_limited` for a free model while the level's free turns are used for now, and `budget_exhausted` while the wallet of the caller's context has spent past its credit.

retention.description: Whether a request on the model can be kept: `none` when no provider that serves it keeps a request, or, while Zero data retention is on, when its requests go only to such providers; `provider` when one may. Absent when not known.

default_environment.description: The environment a manifest that names none runs in, an empty string where the deployment names none.

id.description: The account a create lands in: `p-` and 32 hexadecimal digits for a person's own, `o-` and 32 for an organization's.

labels.description: The labels to write into `metadata.labels` of every manifest you create, as they are.

org_id.description: The organization of the context, an empty string in a person's own.

owner.description: Who owns what you create, the issuer and the token's subject.

code.description: A stable token a program reads.

days.description: Every day of the month in the zone, the 1st first.

items.description: One entry for each of the person's triggers.

last_month_micro.description: What last month spent in all, in the zone, in micro-USD.

person_led_per_day_micro.description: What the person's own conversations spent a day on average over the last 28 days, in micro-USD: what each day ahead is expected to cost them.

pool_micro.description: What proactive work may spend in a rolling 7 days now, in micro-USD, as the spending read's.

proactive_again_at.description: When the pool is spent now: when it frees up, as the oldest proactive spending leaves the 7 days. Adding credit frees it sooner.

proactive_skips_from.description: The first day a run is expected to be skipped because the proactive pool is spent, when that day is in the month; after `proactive_again_at` when the pool is spent now.

proactive_week_micro.description: What proactive work spent in the last 7 days, in micro-USD, as the spending read's.

runs_out_on.description: The day by whose end what is expected from now would pass the credit, when that day is in the month. The person's own spending is still counted after it, at the same rate.

share_bps.description: The share of the credit proactive work may use, in basis points, as the spending read's; assumed for the rest of the month.

spendable_micro.description: The credit the wallet can spend now, in micro-USD, as the spending read's.

unlisted_proactive_micro.description: What proactive work spent this month that no listed item's runs hold, in micro-USD: the person's own replies in a conversation a trigger started, a trigger since deleted, a turn not yet counted. Never below zero.

zone.description: The time zone the month is read in.

expected_person_led_micro.description: What the rest of the day is expected to cost the person's own conversations, in micro-USD; zero on a day that is over.

expected_proactive_micro.description: What the rest of the day's runs are expected to cost, in micro-USD: the runs of the items whose `half` is `proactive` and that name no `counted_in`.

person_led_micro.description: What the person's own conversations spent that day so far, in micro-USD.

proactive_micro.description: What proactive work spent that day so far, in micro-USD: the usage counted, or what the listed items' runs cost that day when that is more.

allowance_skips.description: How many of the expected runs its own allowance would skip.

counted_in.description: For a follow-up in a conversation another listed trigger started: that trigger. Its runs are inside that trigger's month and count toward its allowance.

days.description: Every day of the month in the zone.

expected_at.description: For a schedule, a list of times or a follow-up, the times of its runs expected this month, skipped ones included.

expected_runs.description: How many runs are expected this month, skipped ones included.

fires_on.description: How it runs: on a schedule, when an event arrives, once at a time, as a follow-up does, or once at each time of a list it was given.

forecast_micro.description: What its month comes to: `spent_micro` and the runs expected that are not skipped, in micro-USD; absent with no `per_run_micro`.

half.description: Where its runs are billed: `person_led` for a follow-up, or a trigger continuing one conversation, in a conversation the person started, whose runs their own average already holds.

most_micro.description: With no `per_run_micro`, an allowance and not paused: the most it can spend by the month's end, its allowance over the time left, in micro-USD.

paused.description: It is paused, so nothing more is expected of it.

per_day.description: For a trigger on events, its runs a day over the last 28 days, or since it was made.

per_run_micro.description: The mean cost of its latest five runs that worked, in micro-USD; absent before its first.

per_week_micro.description: Its weekly allowance, in micro-USD; absent without one.

runs.description: How many of its runs worked this month so far.

share_skips.description: How many of the expected runs the proactive pool would skip.

spent_micro.description: What its runs cost this month so far, in micro-USD.

trigger_id.description: The trigger, as the agents' API names it.

expected.description: How many runs are expected the rest of that day.

expected_skipped.description: How many of those would be skipped.

ran.description: How many of its runs worked that day.

skipped.description: How many of its runs were skipped that day, by its allowance or the pool.

ForecastSkipping.description: Where its next run is skipped, or, for a follow-up or a time of a list, waits; absent otherwise. A follow-up a limit stops is kept and runs once the limit lifts, within a day; a time of a list waits the same way within its trigger's lateness bound, and never past the next time of its list.

until.description: Its next run that is not skipped, or when a follow-up or a time of a list that waits runs; absent when none is expected.

why.description: Its weekly allowance is reached, or the proactive pool is spent.

FreeSearches.description: No longer answered. Every web search is charged to the wallet, on every level, Quick included.

bound.description: The free web searches one person makes on Quick in a UTC day.

resets_at.description: When the count resets, the next 00:00 UTC.

used.description: The free web searches the caller made today.

FreeTurns.description: Present where a daily bound on free turns applies to the caller on the level.

bound.description: The turns one person may start on a free model of the level in a day.

used.description: The turns the caller started on a free model of the level today.

Instructions.description: The person's standing instructions, given to each session they start in their personal context, after the agent's own. A change applies from their next session.

text.description: At most `max_chars` characters; text in a script whose characters take three or four bytes in UTF-8 reaches the limit sooner. Empty when not set.

body.description: More detail, on a read of one memory. A memory names another as `[[id]]`.

checksum.description: What `If-Match` names to change it only as it was read.

description.description: The memory itself, in one line.

name.description: A title of a few words.

project.description: The project's id, on a project's memory.

scope.description: Whose memory it is: the person's own, which every conversation in their personal context reads, or a project's, which only that project's conversations read.

sensitive.description: Whether it is about a sensitive topic.

source.description: Where it came from: a conversation's id, `you` for what the person added, or `import`.

updated.description: When it was last saved, on a list.

project.description: The project to move it to, with `scope` `project`.

purges_at.description: When it is gone for good.

skipped.description: How many lines the scope already held.

import_prompt.description: What a person asks another assistant before an import.

max_bytes.description: The most bytes of a memory's file.

max_description.description: The most characters of a memory's description.

max_import_lines.description: The most lines one import saves.

max_name.description: The most characters of a memory's name.

types.description: The groups, in the order a client shows them.

more.description: Whether the folder holds more files than one list reads.

projects.description: The person's projects, by id and name.

chats.description: Search past chats: whether a conversation can search and read the person's other conversations, in a project only that project's. On by default.

remember.description: Remember new things: whether conversations save memories. On by default.

review.description: What happens to what tidying memory changed at night: `apply` applies it and shows the person what changed, `ask` holds it for their OK. `apply` by default.

sensitive.description: Include sensitive topics: whether memories about health, beliefs and the like are kept. Off by default.

deleted_sensitive.description: How many memories marked sensitive this change deleted.

display_name.description: The model's name as a person reads it, such as `DeepSeek V4 Flash` for `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`: what a product says when it tells a person which model answered. Absent when the catalog states none; name the model by `name` then.

name.description: The model's name, as the request named it.

omitted.description: How many serving providers are left out of `served_by`. Present with `retention`.

price.description: The price a request to the model is charged at, so a product can say whether a model that took over a turn costs the same. Absent when the catalog does not hold the model or it carries no price.

retention.description: `none` when no provider that serves the model keeps a request, `provider` when a request may reach one that keeps it under its own terms. Absent when the terms are not known.

served_by.description: The providers that serve the model. Present with `retention`.

Network.description: Which sites a session's machine may reach in the context. The setting applies to every session in the context: the session joins its agent's own hosts, its secrets' hosts and its repositories' hosts to it whatever the mode.

domains.description: The sites added, lower-cased and sorted.

editable.description: Whether the caller may change the setting: always in the personal context, and as an owner or admin in an organization's.

bearer.description: One access token issued by Latere Auth for the audience `api.latere.ai`: a product's actor token for the person it acts for, a platform key's token, or a personal access token. The caller is the token's subject and the context is the token's `org_id`, the personal context when it names none. No cookie is read. A token narrowed by grants is answered only when a grant covers `topos:session.create` or `topos:session.send`, unless a route says otherwise: the routes of a conversation's links and of a trigger's link and address hold it to a grant on that conversation or that trigger instead.

info.description: What a product reads about the person it acts for and that no single capability owns: the Effort levels a session can run at and what the next turn on each costs, the wallet a turn is charged to, adding credit to it and what was spent, by the person and by the work their triggers start, and where a request is processed. A product also makes the person's copy of an agent the platform manages exist here, before it starts their session. And it reads and changes the person's preferences: what to call them, their standing instructions, which sites a session's machine may reach, their pins and bookmarks, and whether conversations may be shared; it makes, lists and stops the read-only links to a conversation a person shares; and it keeps the person's projects, which group their conversations and hold the apps those conversations work on. It also lists, invites and removes the people a private app opens for. And it gives a person's trigger its own link, which another app posts to, or its own email address, which mail is forwarded to, each starting the trigger. It lists, renames and removes the person's own computers, which the sessions they start work on. Every route answers the caller named by the token, in the context the token names.

put.description: Makes the caller's copy of the managed agent `id` exist in the context the token names and carry the live version, then answers it. The copy is an agent of the Agents API named `id`, which a product then starts sessions of with `POST /v1/agents/sessions` and `"agent": id`. A missing copy is created, and a copy the platform manages is brought to the live version; an agent of that name the caller made themselves is never changed. The platform applies the copy with the caller's own token, so the Agents API decides it as the caller. A session keeps the version it started with. In the caller's personal context the apply also gives the person, once, the Always on item Tidy memory, which tidies their memory at night in the time zone `Latere-Time-Zone` names; a person who deletes it is not given it again. The body is empty.

get.description: The people the caller invited to the app, oldest first. An invite no one has accepted yet shows its address alone, in state `pending`; once a person signs in at the app with the invited address it is `active`, and names their account. `organization` is set on an organization's app, whose members always open it. `password` says when the app's password was set, and is null when it has none: a private app with a password also opens for anyone who types it, with no Latere account. `actions` are what the caller may do here: `set_password` is among them where the installation offers app passwords. Where it is absent no password can be set, and one that is set opens nothing until it is offered again; `password` still says it is there, and it can still be removed. `limits` are the bounds of the list and of a password. The list is answered only to those who may change the app's settings: its owner, or an organization's owners and admins. Who may open the app is its general access, set on the app itself: these people are let in when it is private, and anyone with its address when it is public or unlisted.

post.description: Adds addresses to the app's list as viewers, who open the app at its address when it is private, and nothing else of it. A person is let in when they sign in at the app with the invited address, and from then on by their account, whatever address it holds later. Nothing is mailed: the caller sends the app's address to the people they invited. At most 20 addresses a call. The caller's own address and an address already on the list are skipped and listed in `skipped`; when every address is skipped the answer is 200. An app has at most 50 people with access, pending invites included, and a person makes at most 100 invites in 24 hours across their apps.

delete.description: Removes the app's password at once: the app then opens only for its owner, an organization's members and the people invited, each signed in, and every visit made with the password ends within a minute. Removing a password that is not set is no error. A password is removed whether or not the installation still offers setting one.

put.description: Sets the app's password, or replaces the one it has. While the app is private, anyone who opens its address and types the password opens the app and its previews, with no Latere account and no sign-in; its owner, an organization's members and the people invited still sign in. A password is `limits.min_password` to `limits.max_password` characters of the access read, 8 to 128, each Unicode code point counted and nothing trimmed, so spaces count. It is kept as a slow hash and is in no answer afterwards: the caller is the only one who holds it. Replacing a password ends every visit made with the old one within a minute. A password on an app that is public or unlisted opens nothing more, since anyone with the address opens such an app already. A private app that is made unlisted or public loses its password, however the change is made, and the visits made with it end within a minute. Offered where the access read's `actions` name `set_password`.

The person's record is written only when they have none, so the first sign-in that carried a source is the one kept, and the answer is 204 whatever was kept. The platform shows it only when it was written within ten minutes of the account's creation. Only a person's own sign-in records an arrival: a hosted agent's, a service account's and a key's token are refused.

get.description: The three Effort levels, least effort first, as the caller would be answered on each now. A level is asked for by its routed name wherever a session's model is named: an agent's `spec.model.name`, or the `model.name` of a session's model change. `available` says whether a message sent on the level now would be routed for the caller; when it would not, `reason` is the refusal that message would get. `next` says what the next turn on an available level costs: nothing while the level runs a free model, and credit from the wallet of the caller's context otherwise. In a person's own context Quick runs its free models first and, when none can answer, its cheapest model with a price, charged to the caller's wallet like any other level, so its `next.charge` there is `none` while a free model would run and `credit` otherwise; that model is among its `models`. `models` lists the models the level may run for the caller, in its order of preference; a session runs one of them alone when its model is given the routed name `tier/<id>/<model>`, for example `tier/thorough/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`, which keeps the level's reasoning and free turns and is refused `model_tier_model_not_in_level` for a model the level does not list for the caller. The name a person reads for a model is the one `GET /v1/account/data/models` declares. `auto` is present while the installation offers Auto, the routed name `tier/auto`, which picks Quick or Thorough for each message that starts a turn. With `reads` `shape` it picks by length: Quick for a message under 600 characters with no file and no link after a turn that ran no tool, Thorough otherwise. With `reads` `message` it picks by what the message asks, and by length wherever that cannot be read in time. A message with a file or an image, any message after one in the same session, and a message after a turn that ran a tool run at least at Thorough. With `reads` `message`, so does a message that names a service the person connected, such as Gmail or GitHub, and a message that reads or acts on a connected service counts as Thorough work whether or not it names it. Auto never runs Sustained by itself: with `asks` holding `sustained`, a message that looks like a long task and says its client can ask (`askable: true` on the message) is refused `auto_asks_before_sustained` with `limits.suggest`, `tier/sustained`, and `limits.ask`, a token; the client runs it on Sustained by changing the session's model to `tier/sustained` and sending it again, or on Auto, at Thorough, by sending it again with `answers` set to the token. Any other such message runs at Thorough; a session moves down from Thorough only once it has been quiet for a few minutes, and a level that cannot run for the sender is passed over for the other. Each answer on Auto records the level it ran at: the session's model carries it as `route`, in the session and in `session.model_changed`. `tier/auto/<model>` is refused `model_tier_unknown`, since Auto names no model. The answer is computed for each call, counts no turn and posts no credit. Two calls a moment apart may differ. Members are only ever added to a level.

get.description: The runs of the caller's Always on items that change their memory, newest first, at most 50. Tidy memory runs at night, once for the person's own memory and once for each project with something new, and changes each scope's memory: it combines memories that say the same thing, settles ones that contradict each other, and removes ones that only recorded a finished task. `counts` are the memories each run added, updated and removed, applied or waiting, and how many wait for the person. A run under Ask me first, `review` `ask`, waits until the person applies or declines it; a change to a memory the person wrote waits under either mode. What still waits at `expires_at`, 7 days after the run ended, is declined. `state` is `running` until the run ends, then `applied`, `waiting`, `partly_applied`, `declined` or `undone`.

One run with each memory it changed: `before` is the memory's file as it was and `after` as the run left it, each absent for a side there is none of, for a client to show the difference. `name` and `description` are the memory's after the change, or before it for one removed. `held` is `yours` for a change to a memory the person wrote, which waits for their OK whatever the review mode. Each is the folder `files/<name>` of a space, with `name` compared without regard to the case of its letters. Anyone who reads the space opens, downloads and shares what is inside one, and nobody renames, writes or deletes there: Storage refuses such a change with `403` and the reason `reserved_folder` in the detail of its answer. `children` says what a folder directly inside is named after: `session` for a conversation's id, `project` for a project's, and `scope` for memory, whose folders are `you` and `projects`. `readers` says who reads inside one of those: `space` for everyone who reads the rest of the space, and `session` for the people who read that conversation, its starter and the owners and admins of the organization it runs in. A member of an organization who is neither is never listed a `session` folder by Storage, so a client shows them the conversations they read and opens each folder by its own path. `versions` and `trash` say whether a file inside keeps earlier versions and whether a delete inside can be undone. The answer names no space and no person and is the same for every caller. Any token for the audience reads it, a key narrowed to Storage included.

get.description: What the caller will have spent by the end of the calendar month in their time zone, and whether their credit lasts that long. Their own conversations are expected to cost their average a day over the last 28 days, and each trigger of theirs is simulated run by run to the month's end: a schedule at its fire times, a trigger on events at its runs a day over the last 28 days, a follow-up at its time, each run at the mean cost of its latest five. A run is skipped where the trigger's weekly allowance is at or past over the 7 days before it, and where the proactive pool is spent then, the pool being today's share of the credit left at that moment and the week's proactive spend; with no credit left, nothing priced runs. A follow-up in a conversation the person started is billed as their own spending, so it is counted in their half (`half` is `person_led`); one in a conversation another trigger started is inside that trigger's month (`counted_in`). For every day ahead, `expected_proactive_micro` is the expected cost of the items whose `half` is `proactive` and that name no `counted_in`, so those items' months and `unlisted_proactive_micro` add up to the proactive half. The pause of every trigger at once is not applied. The days are the zone's; each hour of spending is counted on the day its start falls on there. The personal context only.

get.description: The caller's spending by day, and where their share for proactive work stands. Proactive work is what runs with nobody watching, counted here by session: what a session a trigger's firing started spends is proactive, and what a session the person started spends is theirs, a turn a wake begins in it included. Each entry of `days` is a UTC day, oldest first and today last, in micro-USD. A share of the person's credit goes to proactive work: `share_bps` is a fifth until the person has spent for 28 days, and then moves once a week halfway toward one less the part of their credit they spent themselves over the last 28 days, between a twentieth and a half. `pool_micro` is that share of `spendable_micro` and `proactive_week_micro`, what proactive work spent in the last 7 days, so what it spent does not shrink its own pool. Once the week's proactive spend reaches the pool, a trigger's firing and a wake start nothing (`proactive_share_spent`) until the oldest spend leaves the 7 days, and a trigger an agent proposes names a weekly allowance no larger than the pool.
